item.title: Pressure intensifies on Carrick as Man Utd lose to Bournemouth
item.description: Manchester United's winless run stretches to eight matches in all competitions as they are beaten 3-0 by Bournemouth at Old Trafford - a defeat that leaves United's manager Michael Carrick under severe pressure.

item.title: Liverpool earn first league win at Anfield with victory over Brighton
item.description: An own goal from Brighton's Pascal Gross swiftly followed by a goal from Alexander Isak, sees Liverpool beat the Seagulls 2-0 at Anfield to move into the Premier League top four.

item.title: Sage continues to struggle as Palace lose at home to Newcastle
item.description: Crystal Palace's winless run stretches to four matches as they are beaten 2-0 at home by Newcastle, leaving the club just a point outside the relegation zone with the pressure mounting on manager Pierre Sage.

item.title: Hull draw third consecutive home game after being held by Brentford
item.description: Hull draw a third consecutive home game after Dango Ouattara's equaliser helps Brentford grab a point in a 1-1 draw at the MKM Stadium in the Premier League.

item.title: Sunderland stay bottom after goalless draw with Leeds
item.description: Sunderland remain bottom of the Premier League after a goalless draw with Leeds in difficult conditions at the Stadium of Light.

item.title: End approaching for Carrick but Man Utd owners' problems far bigger
item.description: Manchester United's fans sang their support for Michael Carrick during the 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth, but voiced their opposition to virtually everything else.

item.title: Isak finally living up to price tag as Liverpool patience rewarded
item.description: Alexander Isak scores his sixth Premier League goal of the season as Liverpool make it four wins out of their last four under Andoni Iraola.

item.title: 'It wasn't a farewell from me' - but horror start leaves Carrick on brink
item.description: Michael Carrick's future as Manchester United manager is under major threat following the home loss to Bournemouth on Sunday.

item.title: Who has made Troy's Premier League team of the week?
item.description: After every round of Premier League matches this season, Troy Deeney gives us his team of the week. Do you agree with his choices?

item.title: Pressure grows on Sage as fans turn on Palace boss
item.description: Crystal Palace boss Pierre Sage had a tough act to follow in Oliver Glasner - and four months into the job the Frenchman is already under big pressure.

item.title: What have Man Utd changed to turn around WSL form?
item.description: It is a different picture at Manchester United now than it was last month - and they proved it to fight back and earn a point against rivals Manchester City.

item.title: Fernandes left on bench for Man Utd defeat - a failed gamble?
item.description: Manchester United skipper Bruno Fernandes is left on the bench for Sunday's 3-0 loss to Bournemouth, following his criticism of manager Michael Carrick.

item.title: Howe open to Man Utd talks - Monday's gossip
item.description: Eddie Howe is open to holding talks with Manchester United if they part ways with manager Michael Carrick, three Premier League clubs are monitoring Bayern Munich's Lennart Karl, plus more.

item.title: Fernandes left out - Man Utd hammered, Bournemouth brilliant - how they rated
item.description: Another catastrophic day for Manchester United and a glorious one for Bournemouth - how did the players rate?

item.title: Carrick 'saddened' by Man Utd situation after Bournemouth loss
item.description: Manchester United manager Micheal Carrick reflects on a 'tough day' after his side lost 3-0 at home to Bournemouth with his future in doubt with United without a win in their last eight games.

item.title: Late own goal gives Liverpool point against London City Lionesses
item.description: A stoppage time own goal from Jana Fernandez sees Liverpool snatch a point against London City Lionesses, as the two sides draw 2-2 in the Women's Super League.

item.title: Vangsgaard scores twice as Villa hang on to beat Everton
item.description: Amalie Vangsgaard scores twice for Aston Villa as the away side survive a late fightback from Everton to win 3-2 at Goodison Park in the Women's Super League.

item.title: Malard stars as Chelsea beat Palace to extend unbeaten start
item.description: Melvine Malard scores twice and wins a penalty as she helps Chelsea come from behind to beat Crystal Palace 3-1 in the Women's Super League, as the away side extend their unbeaten start to the season to seven matches.

item.title: Birmingham get first win of the season after edging past Charlton
item.description: Wilda Leidhammar scores as Birmingham secure their first WSL win this season, beating bottom club Charlton 1-0 at St Andrew's, as the away side's wait for a first point goes on.

item.title: When is Premier League 'sacking season' - and who should be worried?
item.description: As pressure builds on Manchester United manager Michael Carrick, BBC Sport looks at when the Premier League 'sacking season' begins.

item.title: Weir would swap Ballon d'Or nominations for World Cup
item.description: Caroline Weir reflects on her Ballon d'Or nomination while eyeing a World Cup spot with Scotland.

item.title: Sheffield Wednesday sack Pedersen after 15 months
item.description: Sheffield Wednesday sack head coach Henrik Pedersen after less than 15 months in charge following consecutive defeats.

item.title: Dunfermline meet Queen of the South in Scottish Cup
item.description: Last season's finalists Dunfermline Athletic will visit Queen of the South in the third round of the Scottish Cup.

item.title: Chaos or concern - Hanley's striker cameo poses questions for Hibs
item.description: Grant Hanley was called upon to be a makeshift striker for Hibs against Celtic, but what does it signal for the Scottish Premiership's bottom side?

item.title: All you need to know about the 2026 Ballon d'Or
item.description: Our Ask Me Anything team tells you all you need to know about the 70th Ballon d'Or Ceremony.

item.title: What Man Utd need now is stability, not more changes - Pulis
item.description: BBC Sport columnist Tony Pulis explains why Bruno Fernandes' comments after Manchester United's defeat by Como showed how hard it must be to run the club at the moment.

item.title: England win cerebral palsy World Cup for first time
item.description: Sam Dewhirst and David Porcher score the goals as England beat the United States in the final of the Cerebral Palsy World Cup in Atlanta.

item.title: Hayen sacked by Burnley after just 14 games
item.description: Nicky Hayen is sacked after just 14 games in charge at Burnley following a poor start to the season.

item.title: Who am I? Plus today's other quizzes
item.description: Test your ball knowledge against today's Who Am I?, Five in Five and Brainteaser.

item.title: The non-football fan who snapped the game beautifully
item.description: Peter Robinson has been a photographer at 13 FIFA World Cups since 1970.

item.title: Strikers finding form as Rangers bounce back
item.description: Derek McInnes demanded a response from his Rangers team after the disappointment of two dropped points at Dundee - and they delivered in emphatic style against St Johnstone.

item.title: Sutton's predictions v Waffle the Wonder Dog and his owner Simon
item.description: BBC Sport football expert Chris Sutton takes on Waffle the Wonder Dog and his owner Simon, plus the BBC readers and AI with his predictions for this weekend's Premier League fixtures.

item.title: Arsenal relieve pressure with Spurs win - can they kick on now?
item.description: Arsenal end their five-match winless run in the Women's Super League with victory at Tottenham - but can they kick on now?

item.title: Huddersfield on top, but difficult days for Derby - Sam Parkin's EFL takeaways
item.description: BBC Final Score pundit Sam Parkin looks at the weekend's talking points in the EFL, including Huddersfield's fine form and QPR's big win over Swansea.

item.title: Infantino says he is backed by 'vast majority'
item.description: Fifa president Gianni Infantino laughs off questions about whether he considered resigning over the World Cup sell-off debacle.

item.title: Should Palmer have been sent off earlier than he was?
item.description: Match of the Day pundit Martin Keown looks at the red card shown to Cole Palmer during Chelsea's 2-0 defeat to Tottenham, with the former Arsenal defender agreeing with the decision and suggesting Palmer was lucky not to receive a straight red for an early incident.

item.title: How 'special talent' Jackson inspired Villa to victory over Man City
item.description: Match of the Day pundits Martin Keown and Steph Houghton look at the impact Aston Villa forward Nicolas Jackson had with his two goals in their 2-1 victory over Manchester City, with Keown describing him as a "special talent".

item.title: 'Best performance since I arrived' - De Zerbi praises Spurs after win
item.description: Tottenham manager Roberto De Zerbi describes his side's 2-0 victory over Chelsea at Stamford Bridge as "the best since he arrived at the club", adding the win was special given it was against their local rivals.

item.title: Arsenal fight back to beat Tottenham and ease pressure on Slegers
item.description: Alessia Russo scores a controversial penalty as Arsenal come from behind to beat local rivals Tottenham Hotspur 2-1 to secure just their second win of the season in the Women's Super League, and ease the pressure on manager Renee Slegers.

item.title: 'We could have played better' - Alonso disappointed after defeat
item.description: Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso admitted he was disappointed by his side's performance, saying they "could have played better" following their 2-0 defeat by Tottenham at Stamford Bridge.

item.title: Arteta 'delighted' with Arsenal win after 'tough week'
item.description: Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta is "delighted" with his sides performance after making five changes in their 2-0 victory over Everton.

item.title: 'It's harsh' - was Arsenal's winning penalty a controversial decision?
item.description: Following Arsenal's 2-1 win at rivals Tottenham Hotspur, former England footballers Ellen White, Fara Williams and Alex Scott discuss whether the away side were fortunate to be given a penalty, which proved to be the winning moment for Arsenal.

item.title: Symonds scores screamer as Brighton beat West Ham
item.description: Maisie Symonds scores a 'goal of the season' contender to help Brighton beat West Ham 3-0, securing just their second league win of the season in the Women's Super League.

item.title: Forest left frustrated as winless run goes on after draw at Ipswich
item.description: Nottingham Forest ended a run of three successive league defeats but endured another night of missed chances as they drew 1-1 at Ipswich Town in the Premier League, but the result does move the away side out of the relegation zone on goal difference.

item.title: Goal, assist... goal-kick - Kane underlines Ballon d'Or credentials
item.description: Why Declan Rice backs his England team-mate Harry Kane to win the Ballon d'Or after Arsenal's draw with Bayern Munich in the Champions League.

item.title: Spurs boss Ho wants 'more support and training' for WSL referees
item.description: Tottenham manager Martin Ho was frustrated by a penalty decision in their defeat by Arsenal and says Women's Super League referees "need more support".

item.title: The keeper doing 'Premier League' things for EFL's last unbeaten side
item.description: Walsall goalkeeper Jed Ward is producing "Premier League" contributions with his hands and feet, say dazzled team-mates and his manager.

item.title: Beer & Blackpool beach was how British players bonded - Pulis
item.description: BBC Sport columnist Tony Pulis explains what Spurs will get from their team-bonding trip to Spain, and how differently managers built team morale in his day.

item.title: Do Manchester City have any grounds to win their appeal?
item.description: Manchester City face "substantial hurdles" to overcome if they are to have any chance of winning their appeal after being found guilty of breaking the Premier League's financial rules, a leading lawyer has told BBC Sport.
